description:
Found during the bedrock-287 audit; pre-existing.

`do_remove_worker/2` (lib/bedrock/service/foreman/impl.ex:111-114) and `do_remove_workers/2` (:129) both call `recompute_health/1` but neither calls `notify_waiting_for_healthy/1`. Only `do_worker_health/3` (:241-246) pairs the two.

## Failure scenario

A foreman hosts two workers; one failed to start, so health is `{:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}`. A caller invokes `wait_for_healthy/2` (default timeout `:infinity`) and parks in `waiting_for_healthy`. An operator removes the failed worker. `recompute_health/1` flips health to `:ok` — and the parked caller is never told. It blocks forever even though the condition it waited for now holds.

Same shape as bedrock-mxt (spin-up settling health without waking waiters), but on the removal path.

## Fix

Pipe `notify_waiting_for_healthy/1` after `recompute_health/1` on both removal paths. Consider making the pairing structural — a single `settle_health/1` helper that both recomputes and notifies — so a future call site cannot recompute without waking waiters.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Park a fake `{self(), tag}` in `waiting_for_healthy`, remove the only failing worker, assert the state's `waiting_for_healthy` is emptied and `assert_receive {^tag, :ok}`.
title: [BUG] Worker removal recomputes foreman health but never wakes wait_for_healthy callers
